canDo: Can state causes, results and purposes clearly, forming a 2–3-step chain of reasoning.
review: Review parce que; extend to puisque/donc/c’est pourquoi, and add afin de / pour que.
input: Listening: cause and effect in the environment/daily life; reading: a short explanatory text.
output: Write 130 words: problem – cause – result; explain a choice aloud in 2 minutes.
checkpoint: At least 2 kinds of cause/effect link in the same paragraph; logically correct relations.
challenge: Today’s challenge: in RFI’s Journal en français facile, find a news item about the environment and write it up in 3 sentences as “cause → result → purpose” (parce que / donc / pour que or pour + infinitive); then add one sentence about something green you can do in your own life.

questions.why: The reason given is that we spend about 85% of our time indoors. The sources are many; the text doesn’t say they are necessarily more toxic.
The ending is explicit: ten minutes of airing won’t cool the walls.
« quand les plantes sont au repos » is the reason given; saturated soil actually prevents water from soaking in.
« contrairement à ce que supposaient de nombreux riverains » — the culprit is uneven wheels caused by old brakes.
« un quart du trafic mais l'essentiel des plaintes » — note that the two proportions refer to different things.
« Leur coût, en revanche, dépasse le budget disponible », so sections with homes within fifty metres come first.
The ending says the priority is the places minérales, not along the avenues.
« Ce qui tue, c'est le cumul »; each factor on its own is often bearable.
It refers to the two months, June to August, when there are no flowers to forage once the rapeseed has finished flowering.
He sets out the cost of doing nothing: rising heating bills, a ban on letting from 2028, a lower resale value.
8 of the 22 flats are let, and class F can’t be let from 2028.
Braking distance at fifty km/h is almost twice that at thirty.
